model_annotation: The plot illustrates how classification accuracy (ACC) varies with the co-occurrence number for six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and is shown on a logarithmic scale, with major tick labels at approximately 0, 10¹, 10², and 10³; the plotted points appear at four co-occurrence values spanning from the low single digits (around 5) to the low thousands (around 3000). The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale, ranging from roughly 38% up to about 66%, with labeled ticks at regular 5% intervals (40, 45, 50, 55, 60, 65). The Base line is black with circular markers and a solid line, rising from about 38–39% at the smallest co-occurrence value to about 44% at the largest (with intermediate points around ~42% and ~44%). FT is blue with downward triangle markers and a solid line, increasing from about 40% to about 48% across the x-range (with midpoints around ~43–44% and ~46%). IKE is red with upward triangle markers and a solid line, moving from roughly 43% at the smallest x value to roughly 49–50% at the largest (with intermediate values near ~45% and ~47%). MEND is brown with diamond markers and a solid line, increasing from about 44–45% to about 56–57% (with intermediate values near ~49% and ~54%). MEMIT is purple with circular markers and a solid line, rising from about 44% to about 55% (with intermediate values near ~51% and ~53%). ROME is green with square markers and a solid line, increasing from about 51% at the smallest co-occurrence value to about 66% at the largest, passing through intermediate values around ~57% and ~62%.
